items.name: Florida Recreation Development Assistance Program (FRDAP)
items.pays: Buying or building land for public outdoor recreation — parks, trails, playgrounds, boat and beach access.
items.who: Counties, cities, towns and special districts that run public recreation sites.
items.match: Depends on project size (see the application guide).
items.note: Due 5:00 p.m. EDT, through the DEP Grantee Portal only (Google Chrome required). This cycle funds FY2027-28 and depends on the Legislature’s budget.

items.name: Resilient Florida Grant Program
items.pays: Projects that protect critical assets from flooding and sea level rise, and the vulnerability studies that come first.
items.who: Counties, cities and towns, certain special districts, and regional resilience groups. Implementation projects require a finished vulnerability assessment.
items.size: Not stated on the program page.
items.match: Not stated on the program page.
items.note: The 2026 portal was open July 1 – September 1, 2026. Watch for the 2027 cycle.

items.name: Waterways Assistance Program
items.pays: Channel dredging, boat ramps, shoreline stabilization, fishing piers, waterway education, boating safety.
items.who: Cities, counties, port authorities and special taxing districts in the District’s 12 counties, including Brevard.
items.size: About $10–12 million a year across the District; capped at 90% of the FIND tax the county pays.
items.match: FIND pays up to 75% for public navigation projects and up to 50% for other projects.
items.note: Applications open in January and are due by the end of March; awards are announced in October.

items.name: Florida Boating Improvement Program
items.agency: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
items.pays: Boat ramps, docks, moorings, channel markers and boating education.
items.who: Counties, cities and other government bodies.
items.size: Not stated on the program page.
items.match: Not stated on the program page.
items.note: “The next application period will be announced in 2027.”

items.name: Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC)
items.agency: Florida Division of Emergency Management (FEMA money)
items.pays: Projects that lower damage from future disasters — drainage, flood protection, stronger buildings.
items.who: State agencies, local governments and tribes, through the state.
items.match: Federal share up to 75%; up to 90% for small, impoverished communities.
items.note: Notices of interest were due August 14, 2026.
